d: Eight years after the infamous Cape Town Test, Usman Khawaja has reopened one of the darkest chapters in Australian cricket. In his autobiography, Sabr, the former Australia opener claims the entire dressing room knew about Sandpapergate, questioning why Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were left to shoulder the blame. His revelations also contradict the accounts of Australia's bowling group, including Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon. With questions over collective responsibility, Nic Maddinson's response and the timing of Khawaja's book, Rupha Ramani examines the…
